metadata.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

problem.value: Transformers suffer from computational inefficiency on long sequences due to quadratic scaling with respect to the window length.

evidence.quote: An enormous body of research has appeared on more efficient variants of attention to overcome these drawbacks (Tay, Dehghani, Bahri, et al. 2022), but often at the expense of the very properties that makes it effective.

problem.value: Subquadratic-time architectures like SSMs have been less effective at modeling discrete, information-dense data such as text.

evidence.quote: However, they have been less effective at modeling discrete and information-dense data such as text.

contributions.value: Designing a simple selection mechanism by parameterizing SSM parameters based on the input.

evidence.quote: Building on intuition based on important synthetic tasks such as selective copy and induction heads, we design a simple selection mechanism by parameterizing the SSM parameters based on the input.

contributions.value: Developing a hardware-aware recurrent algorithm using a scan that avoids materializing the expanded state.

evidence.quote: We overcome this with a hardware-aware algorithm that computes the model recurrently with a scan instead of convolution, but does not materialize the expanded state in order to avoid IO access between different levels of the GPU memory hierarchy.

contributions.value: Introducing Mamba, a simplified homogeneous neural network architecture combining selective state spaces with Transformer MLP blocks.

evidence.quote: We simplify prior deep sequence model architectures by combining the design of prior SSM architectures (Dao, Fu, Saab, et al. 2023) with the MLP block of Transformers into a single block, leading to a simple and homogenous architecture design (Mamba) incorporating selective state spaces.
On language modeling, our Mamba-3B model outperforms Transformers of the same size and matches Transformers twice its size, both in pretraining and downstream evaluation.

Mamba out-performs prior state-of-the-art models such as SaShiMi, Hyena, and Transformers on modeling audio waveforms and DNA sequences, both in pretraining quality and downstream metrics (e.g. reducing FID on a challenging speech generation dataset by more than half).

Mamba out-performs prior state-of-the-art models such as SaShiMi, Hyena, and Transformers on modeling audio waveforms and DNA sequences, both in pretraining quality and downstream metrics (e.g. reducing FID on a challenging speech generation dataset by more than half).

method_summary.value: The proposed Mamba architecture combines the H3 block and MLP block into a single homogeneous block, repeating it with normalization and residual connections.

evidence.quote: We simplify this architecture by combining these two components into one, which is stacked homogenously (Figure 3).

method_summary.value: A selection mechanism is introduced by making parameters such as B, C, and Delta functions of the input, turning the model into a time-varying SSM.

evidence.quote: The main difference is simply making several parameters Δ, B, C functions of the input, along with the associated changes to tensor shapes throughout.

method_summary.value: A hardware-aware algorithm is used to compute selective SSMs efficiently on GPUs by leveraging kernel fusion, parallel scan, and recomputation to avoid materializing the full expanded state.

evidence.quote: We address this with three classical techniques: kernel fusion, parallel scan, and recomputation.

method_summary.value: The model uses real values as the default for the state h, alongside initialization strategies derived from prior SSM and HIPPO theory.

evidence.quote: We use real values as the default, which work well for all but one of our tasks; we hypothesize that the complex-real tradeoff is related to the continuous-discrete spectrum in data modalities, where complex numbers are helpful for continuous modalities (e.g. audio, video) but not discrete (e.g. text, DNA).

novelty.value: The authors introduce a selection mechanism to state space models, removing the linear time invariance (LTI) constraint to allow input-dependent dynamics.

evidence.quote: However, a core insight of this work is that LTI models have fundamental limitations in modeling certain types of data, and our technical contributions involve removing the LTI constraint while overcoming the efficiency bottlenecks.

novelty.value: A novel hardware-aware algorithm avoids full state materialization through recomputation and kernel fusion, enabling efficient selective SSM computations.

evidence.quote: We overcome this with a hardware-aware algorithm that exploits the memory hierarchy on modern hardware (Section 3.3).

evidence.quote: For baselines, we compare against the standard Transformer architecture (GPT3 architecture), as well as the strongest Transformer recipe we know of (here referred to as Transformer++), based on the PaLM and LLaMa architectures (e.g. rotary embedding, SwiGLU MLP, RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, no linear bias, and higher learning rates).

For baselines, we compare against the standard Transformer architecture (GPT3 architecture), as well as the strongest Transformer recipe we know of (here referred to as Transformer++), based on the PaLM and LLaMa architectures (e.g. rotary embedding, SwiGLU MLP, RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, no linear bias, and higher learning rates).
We compare against the most well-known open source models at these sizes, most importantly Pythia (Biderman et

al. 2023) and RWKV (B.Peng et al. 2023) which were trained with the same tokenizer, dataset, and training length (300B tokens) as our models.(Note that Mamba and Pythia are trained with context length 2048, while RWKV was trained with context length 1024.)
Figure 5 (Left) shows that Mamba's pretraining perplexity improves smoothly with model size, and that Mamba scales better than both HyenaDNA and Transformer++.

claims.value: Mamba achieves 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers.

evidence.quote: Mamba enjoys fast inference (5× higher throughput than Transformers) and linear scaling in sequence length, and its performance improves on real data up to million-length sequences.

claims.value: Mamba-3B matches the quality of Transformers twice its size on language modeling.

evidence.quote: On language modeling, our Mamba-3B model outperforms Transformers of the same size and matches Transformers twice its size, both in pretraining and downstream evaluation.

claims.value: The hardware-aware algorithm is up to 3x faster on A100 GPUs compared to previous methods.

evidence.quote: The resulting implementation is faster than previous methods both in theory (scaling linearly in sequence length, compared to pseudo-linear for all convolution-based SSMs) and on modern hardware (up to 3× faster on A100 GPUs).

claims.value: Mamba reduces FID on a challenging speech generation dataset by more than half.

evidence.quote: Mamba out-performs prior state-of-the-art models such as SaShiMi, Hyena, and Transformers on modeling audio waveforms and DNA sequences, both in pretraining quality and downstream metrics (e.g. reducing FID on a challenging speech generation dataset by more than half).

claims.value: Mamba-3B scores 4 points higher on average on common sense reasoning compared to Pythia-3B and exceeds Pythia-7B.

evidence.quote: Our Mamba language model has 5× generation throughput compared to Transformers of similar size, and Mamba-3B's quality matches that of Transformers twice its size (e.g. 4 points higher avg. on common sense reasoning compared to Pythia-3B and even exceeding Pythia-7B).
